name: fairy-stockfish
desc: Strong open source chess variant engine (with largeboards support)
why: A chess engine for fairy variants with large boards opens a door into the wild world of chess-like games and their search.

brief.what_it_is: Fairy-Stockfish is a chess variant engine derived from Stockfish. It plays regional, historical, and modern chess variants such as Xiangqi, Janggi, Shogi, Makruk, Crazyhouse, and Atomic, plus games with user-defined rules loaded from a configuration file. It has no graphical interface of its own. It takes a position and a game's rules and returns moves and evaluations through standard engine protocols (UCI, UCCI, USI, UCI-cyclone, CECP/XBoard), so a chess GUI can drive it. The README also describes Python, JavaScript, and WebAssembly bindings that expose move generation, SAN and FEN handling, and game-end checks.
brief.why_it_exists: The README states the goal as "to create an engine supporting a large variety of chess-like games, equipped with the powerful search of Stockfish." It is meant to be easily extended with more games.
brief.how_it_works: It is a fork of Stockfish's search with rule support for many variants, so one engine covers many games. Variants are defined either in built-in code or through a variant configuration file (the README points to src/variants.ini and the wiki). Optional NNUE neural-network evaluation files, which the README says can significantly raise playing strength, are loaded separately.
brief.install_notes: Prebuilt downloads are available for Windows (fairy-stockfish-largeboard_x86-64.exe) and Linux (fairy-stockfish-largeboard_x86-64) from the latest GitHub release, or you can compile from source. No Homebrew-specific notes were given. The program has no GUI, so you will need a compatible chess GUI or play online at pychess, lishogi, or lichess. Optional NNUE network files are listed on the project site. Regional variants Xiangqi, Janggi, and Makruk have dedicated releases with built-in NNUE networks in a separate repository. The README's source-compile instructions were not in the text I fetched.
brief.standout: One engine covers a very wide range of chess-like games, from Xiangqi and Shogi to user-defined rule sets, while keeping Stockfish's search. The README claims it is the world's strongest engine in Janggi, Crazyhouse, and S-Chess, and it supports five GUI protocols, so it works with almost any variant GUI.
brief.status: unknown. The GitHub README has CI badges and links to a 'latest release' page, but I saw no release or commit dates. The homepage lists a 'Fairy-Stockfish 14.0.1 XQ' post and a 'New website' post, but shows no dates on either. The homepage post says the site 'just came to life today' and 'is still under construction'.
brief.caveats: No GUI is included; you need a separate chess GUI or an online site. The README gives no install commands for source builds, so compiling is probably the hard part. Licensed under GPLv3, so distributed binaries must come with source or a pointer to it. The homepage says the site is under construction. The README's 'Compiling Stockfish yourself' section was not in the text I got.
quotes: The program comes without a graphical user interface, so you perhaps want to use it together with a compatible GUI
Despite its generality the playing strength is on a very high level in almost all supported variants, especially when using NNUE.
The goal of the project is to create an engine supporting a large variety of chess-like games, equipped with the powerful search of Stockfish.

judge.reason: A configurable Stockfish-derived engine that searches historical, regional, and user-defined chess variants turns obscure rule systems into playable experiments.

entry.title: Fairy-Stockfish
entry.tldr: A Stockfish-derived engine that plays Xiangqi, Shogi, Janggi, Crazyhouse and any chess-like game you define in a config file.
entry.deeper_look:
Fairy-Stockfish takes the search code from Stockfish and generalises the rules underneath it. One engine plays regional games such as Xiangqi, Janggi, Shogi and Makruk, modern variants such as Crazyhouse and Atomic, and games whose rules you write yourself. It has no interface of its own. It reads a position and a rule set, then returns moves and evaluations over standard engine protocols: UCI, UCCI, USI, UCI-cyclone and CECP/XBoard. A chess GUI is meant to drive it.

The README states the goal as "to create an engine supporting a large variety of chess-like games, equipped with the powerful search of Stockfish." Variants are defined in built-in code or in a variant configuration file (the README points to src/variants.ini and the wiki). Optional NNUE neural-network evaluation files are loaded separately, and the README says they can raise playing strength significantly.

The idea underneath is that a game's rules are data. Change the board size, the pieces, the movement and the win conditions, and the same alpha-beta search still plays well. Writing your own variant and watching a strong engine play it is a quick way into how game search works, and into the large family of chess-like games.

The README also describes Python, JavaScript and WebAssembly bindings that expose move generation, SAN and FEN handling, and game-end checks.
entry.install:
brew install fairy-stockfish
# No GUI is included. Pair it with a UCI-compatible chess GUI, or play online at pychess, lishogi or lichess. Optional NNUE network files are listed on the project site.
